title: Fidelity Contract Simulator — Design & Billing Hooks
author: Maya Hernandez
content:
Overview

This design document describes the Fidelity Contract Simulator, a service and SDK bundle that lets product, sales, and platform teams simulate how changes to fidelity policies, fallbacks, and billing hooks affect customer consumption, invoices, and SLO alignment. The simulator is intended as an offline and interactive evaluation environment for staged pricing and fidelity experiments prior to production rollout.

Goals

- Provide a deterministic simulation engine that ingests historical or synthetic request traces and applies fidelity policies, fallback rules, and billing-credit rules to produce: per-tenant cost projections, per-route SLO impact, and invoice-ready line items.
- Support rapid iteration: product can author policy changes (JSON), run scenarios, and get side-by-side comparisons.
- Surface metrics and traces that map back to runtime telemetry (so simulation results are explainable and auditable).

Non-goals

- The simulator is not a replacement for production billing. It will not emit legal invoices.
- It will not run at production serving scale; batch-mode performance sufficient for daily experiments is acceptable.

Motivation and Use Cases

- Product and pricing teams need to understand revenue and customer impact for proposed fidelity credit rules (e.g., per-token multipliers for high-fidelity outputs).
- Sales and customer success teams need an evidence artifact to show customers how a planned fidelity transition will change monthly spend.
- Engineering needs to validate that fallback and quantization rules do not cause large, unexpected SLO violations at scale.

High-level architecture

1) Input Layer
   - Trace format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) where each event contains: request_id, tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, prompt_tokens, gen_tokens, timestamp_ms, client_region, session_id, response_quality_score (optional).
   - Synthetic trace generator for controlled experiments (parameterized by arrival distribution, sequence length distribution, and percentage of high-fidelity calls).

2) Policy Engine
   - Policies authored as small JSON objects: fidelity_profile, fallback_matrix, quantization_profile, per-route multipliers, per-tenant overrides, and grace windows.
   - Support policy composition: baseline product policy + tenant override + experiment shim.

3) Execution Engine (Simulator Core)
   - Simulates request routing, model variant selection, and cost accounting.
   - Models: each model variant includes attributes { base_cost_per_token_usd, latency_estimate_ms, kv_cache_effectiveness_pct }. These attributes are inputs to the engine and can be overridden per-run.

4) Billing Hooks & Line-item Generator
   - Emulates billing pipeline: per-request cost calculation, discount rules, fidelity-credit escrow simulation, prorations and rounding rules.
   - Output: invoice-ready CSV/JSON lines plus a human-readable reconciliation report.

5) Telemetry & Explainability Layer
   - Produces: aggregated time-series (cost, tokens, latency), per-tenant SLO violation table, and a mapping of simulated events to runtime telemetry keys for later reconciliation.

API & UX surface

- CLI: simulator run --trace traces/tenant-2029-10.ndjson --policy policies/onboarding-experiment.json --output runs/run-2029-11-10/
- Web sandbox (future): upload trace, select policy, run, and view visualization.

Input schema example (NDJSON line):

{
  "request_id": "req_24c8f6",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_acme",
  "route_id": "chat-compose/v1",
  "model_variant": "rwd-llm-13b-hq",
  "prompt_tokens": 42,
  "gen_tokens": 128,
  "timestamp_ms": 1700000000123,
  "client_region": "us-west-2",
  "session_id": "sess_8a7f",
  "response_quality_score": 0.92
}

Policy JSON example (abridged):

{
  "name": "onboarding-60pct-hq",
  "fidelity_profile": {"hq": {"multiplier": 1.5, "max_tokens": 2048}, "std": {"multiplier": 1.0, "max_tokens": 4096}},
  "fallback_matrix": {"hq": ["std","low"]},
  "credits": {"escrow_pct": 0.10, "proration_window_days": 30}
}

Billing model details

- Per-token base price: exporter receives base_cost_per_token_usd from model catalog. The simulator multiplies tokens by base price, then applies fidelity multipliers, per-route multipliers, and tenant discounts.
- Escrow simulation: when a fidelity-credit escrow is configured, the simulator will allocate 'escrowed' credits during the billing period and then simulate release/rollback events (for quality regressions).
- Rounding/proration: the simulator offers both banker's rounding and floor rounding options—selectable per-run to match target billing backends.

Reconciliation outputs

- run-summary.json (aggregate metrics: total_cost_usd, total_prompt_tokens, total_gen_tokens, avg_latency_ms, sla_violations_count)
- invoice-lines.csv (tenant, billing_period_start, billing_period_end, line_description, quantity, unit_price, line_total_usd)
- anomaly-report.md (top 10 routes with highest per-token cost delta vs baseline)

Telemetry & observability mapping

- Simulator creates a mapping file that pairs simulated events with production metric keys used by the console (e.g., route:chat-compose/v1 -> telemetry_key:route_chat_compose_v1).
- Exporter: Prometheus-like timeseries via CSV for offline plotting and a JSON payload compatible with the Console telemetry ingestion test API.

SLOs and thresholds used for experiments

- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 150ms for conversational routes in the baseline profile. Simulator will flag routes where simulated p95 exceeds this.
- Cost delta threshold: experiments that change a tenant's monthly projected spend by > 15% must include an automated pre-approval step.
- Fallback frequency tolerance: if a fidelity policy triggers fallback for > 5% of calls over a 24h window, escalate to engineering review.

Runbook for common scenarios (numbered steps)

1. Prepare trace: export 7 days of anonymized trace from observability (see export-tooling README) and convert to NDJSON format.
2. Pick baseline: select current active policy and model catalog snapshot (catalog_v2029_11_01).
3. Author experiment policy: copy baseline and modify fidelity_profile and credits block.
4. Execute simulation: simulator run --trace traces/week.ndjson --policy experiments/expA.json --catalog sample_catalog.json --output runs/expA/
5. Validate outputs: run-summary.json should be within expectations. If anomalies exist, open a triage ticket with run artifacts attached.

Rollout plan (staged)

- Stage 0 (internal): alpha prototype used by Product & Pricing; manual runs only.
- Stage 1 (sandbox): web UI for non-engineers; outputs suitable for customer-facing summaries; internal-only.
- Stage 2 (preflight): integrate with CI for PR gating on policy changes; small-sample automated runs per commit.
- Stage 3 (audit): tie simulator outputs to billing analysts for final sign-off prior to production policy deployment.

Security, data handling and compliance

- Traces must be anonymized: tenant IDs can be hashed; PII must be removed before upload. The simulator includes a local scrubbing tool.
- Access control: CLI runs require role-based ACLs; sandbox web requires SSO + whitelisting.
- Audit logs: every run stores metadata (user, policy, trace hash, run_id) in the audit index for 365 days.

Performance and scaling expectations

- Target batch run time: 24 hours of 2029 traffic for 10k requests/min peak should complete within 60 minutes on a 16 vCPU, 64GB RAM runner (offline, cached model attributes).
- Memory: simulator keeps per-tenant aggregates in memory; runs should be shardable by tenant for large customers.

Compatibility & migration notes

- Policy format v1 is backward-compatible with legacy pricing configs; conversion tooling included.
- Plan for v2 policy schema that separates fidelity gating from billing multipliers — migration guide will be published with the v2 spec.

Appendix A — Example outputs (excerpt)

Open questions & action items

- Q1: Should the simulator adopt the exact production rounding rules for all customers or provide configurable modes? (Action: Product & Finance to align — target: 2030-02-01)
- Q2: How to surface quality-regression proofs for customers when fidelity credits are escrowed? (Action: Legal & CS to draft customer communication template.)

Notes

This design is intended to be an actionable spec for an MVP that supports weekly experimentation and preflight checks for fidelity-based pricing changes. The immediate next steps are: build a CLI MVP, author three canonical experiment policies, and onboard Pricing and two pilot tenants for validation.
